title: HubSpot BigCommerce Integration Setup Without Code
summary: HubSpot BigCommerce integration uses no-code trigger-and-action workflows to sync data. New orders in BigCommerce automatically update HubSpot contacts.
body_markdown:
## Build the order-to-contact workflow in Activepieces step by step


Connect both accounts, load sample data from a BigCommerce trigger, map the order fields into a HubSpot contact action, then test, check HubSpot and publish.


### Connect your HubSpot and BigCommerce accounts


Create the connections before you add any steps, so a failed authorization shows up on its own instead of inside a half-built flow.


Open Connections in Activepieces, add one for HubSpot and one for BigCommerce, and authorize each with the account that owns the data you want to move.


If you authorize HubSpot with a user who can't create contacts, the connection will save without complaint and the failure will only appear when the action runs.


### Stage 2: add the trigger and load sample data


Add a trigger step, choose the BigCommerce integration, and pick the order event from its trigger list. If the event you need isn't in that list, use the webhook trigger instead and point a BigCommerce webhook at the URL Activepieces gives you.


The screenshot below uses a demo trigger from the Ice-cream integration, "new flavor created", rather than a BigCommerce one.


It's still the panel you'll work in: the trigger name, the connection with its Reconnect button, and a Generate Sample Data section with a Load data button.


Until you press Load data, nothing downstream has a real order to map against.


You can also skip the clicking: describe the job to the built-in chat in Activepieces, say a new BigCommerce order creating or updating a HubSpot contact by email, and it builds and publishes the flow you would otherwise have assembled by hand.


That flow sits under the same RBAC, audit logs and run traces as every hand-built one, so each run leaves a trace anyone on the team can read, with **no certification needed to follow it** . You don't hire for this, you describe it.


MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production.


### Stage 3: map fields into HubSpot


Add the HubSpot step that creates or updates a contact. Click into each field and pick the matching value from the trigger's sample data: the customer email, first name and last name from the order.


Map email first, because it's what HubSpot uses to tell contacts apart. If it's empty on some orders, you'll create duplicates or get failed runs.


1. Run the test on the HubSpot step and read the output it returns, not just the green tick.
2. Open HubSpot and find the contact by email. Confirm each mapped field landed in the property you intended.
3. Fix any field that is blank or misplaced, and re-test.
4. Publish only once a real contact has appeared correctly.


**A passing test against sample data proves your mapping, not your live webhook, so place one real order afterward and confirm it arrives.**
